    customers_list = instance["customer_ids"]
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    vehicle_hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", 0)

    customers = customers_list[:]  # keep deterministic order
    n = len(customers)
    if n == 0:
        return []

    # --- Helpers ---
    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for v in route:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

    def route_distance(route):
        if not route:
            return 0
        d = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            d += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return d

    # Build initial routes: each customer alone
    # route_id -> route list
    routes = []
    load = []
    where_route = [-1] * len(matrix)  # node -> route id
    for cid in customers:
        rid = len(routes)
        routes.append([cid])
        load.append(demands[cid])
        where_route[cid] = rid

    # --- Clarke-Wright savings merges (deterministic) ---
    # Savings for ordered pair (i,j) where i != j
    # Typical: merge route ending at i with route starting at j
    savings = []
    for idx_i in range(n):
        i = customers[idx_i]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for idx_j in range(n):
            if idx_j == idx_i:
                continue
            j = customers[idx_j]
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            # tie-breaker: prefer smaller indices deterministically
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1], -x[2]), reverse=True)

    # Utility to check if node is at start/end of its route
    def is_route_end(rid, node):
        r = routes[rid]
        return node == r[0], node == r[-1]

    def can_merge(rid_a, rid_b, a_end_is_last, b_end_is_first):
        # We want to merge ...i + j...
        if rid_a == rid_b:
            return False
        if a_end_is_last and b_end_is_first:
            # i at end of A, j at start of B => A + B
            new_load = load[rid_a] + load[rid_b]
            return new_load <= capacity
        if (not a_end_is_last) and (not b_end_is_first):
            # i at start of A, j at end of B => reverse(A) + reverse(B) to align => A' end + B' start
            new_load = load[rid_a] + load[rid_b]
            return new_load <= capacity

    active_count = len(routes)
    max_routes = vehicle_hint if isinstance(vehicle_hint, int) and vehicle_hint > 0 else len(routes)

    customers_list = instance["customer_ids"]
    demands = instance["demands"]
    capacity = instance["capacity"]
    matrix = instance["distance_matrix"]
    vehicle_hint = instance.get("vehicle_count_hint", 0)

    n = len(customers)
    if n == 0:
        return []

    def route_load(route):
        s = 0
        for v in route:
            s += demands[v]
        return s

        if not route:
            return 0
        d = matrix[depot][route[0]] + matrix[route[-1]][depot]
        for i in range(len(route) - 1):
            d += matrix[route[i]][route[i + 1]]
        return d

    # route_id -> route list
    routes = []
    load = []
    where_route = [-1] * len(matrix)  # node -> route id

        routes.append([cid])
        load.append(demands[cid])
        where_route[cid] = rid

    # Savings for ordered pair (i,j) where i != j
    # Typical: merge route ending at i with route starting at j
    savings = []
    for idx_i in range(n):
        i = customers[idx_i]
        di = matrix[depot][i]
        for idx_j in range(n):
            if idx_j == idx_i:
                continue
            j = customers[idx_j]
            s = di + matrix[depot][j] - matrix[i][j]
            # tie-breaker: prefer smaller indices deterministically
            savings.append((s, i, j))
    savings.sort(key=lambda x: (x[0], -x[1], -x[2]), reverse=True)

    # Utility to check if node is at start/end of its route
    def is_route_end(rid, node):
        r = routes[rid]
        return node == r[0], node == r[-1]

    def can_merge(rid_a, rid_b, a_end_is_last, b_end_is_first):
        # We want to merge ...i + j...
        if rid_a == rid_b:
            return False
        if a_end_is_last and b_end_is_first:
            # i at end of A, j at start of B => A + B
            new_load = load[rid_a] + load[rid_b]
            return new_load <= capacity
        if (not a_end_is_last) and (not b_end_is_first):
            # i at start of A, j at end of B => reverse(A) + reverse(B) to align => A' end + B' start
            new_load = load[rid_a] + load[rid_b]
            return new_load <= capacity
        return False

    active = set(range(len(routes)))
    active_count = len(routes)
    max_routes = vehicle_hint if isinstance(vehicle_hint, int) and vehicle_hint > 0 else len(routes)

    # Perform merges
    for s, i, j in savings:
        rid_i = where_route[i]
        rid_j = where_route[j]
        if rid_i < 0 or rid_j < 0 or rid_i == rid_j:
            continue
        if rid_i not in active or rid_j not in active:
            continue

        i_start, i_end = is_route_end(rid_i, i)
        j_start, j_end = is_route_end(rid_j, j)

        merged = False
        # Case 1: i is at end of A and j at start of B => A + B
        if i_end and j_start and can_merge(rid_i, rid_j, True, True):
            if active_count > max_routes or max_routes <= 0:
                # still allow merges to reduce number of routes if hint too low; feasibility dominates
                pass
            # Apply merge deterministically
            routes[rid_i].extend(routes[rid_j])
            load[rid_i] += load[rid_j]
            # Update where_route for nodes in B
            for v in routes[rid_j]:
